title: Orphan Claim — Notifier (no Internal) + Parties + Location (Loss → Parties → Location → Summary)
walkthroughSteps: Apply an AC — banner pushes FNOL state into orphan path
Land on /fnol/skeleton-create — left nav shows 4 steps (Loss / Parties / Location / Summary)
Fill Client + Reason on Loss page
Optional: pick Broker or Insured as notifier — Internal is not offered (internal staff register the claim, they never are the notifier)
Click 'Next' — navigate to /fnol/skeleton-parties (starts empty; broker carried over if one was selected)
Optionally add another party (e.g. a different insurer), then click 'Next' — navigate to /fnol/skeleton-location
Enter a location manually (no linked policy, so no 'select from contract' option), then click 'Next' — navigate to /fnol/skeleton-summary
Review Loss + Parties + Notifier blocks, click 'Create' to register the skeleton claim

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Notifier section uses a Broker / Insured radio — Internal is not offered
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: On the **Loss information** page of the orphan flow, a *radio toggle* picks the notifier type (`Broker` / `Insured`) — only the relevant input renders below. Picking **Broker** opens the *Search broker* modal (Name management — IPM-backed). Picking **Insured** shows a single free-text input. **Internal is intentionally excluded**: internal staff (adjuster/colleague) can register the claim but are never the notifier — the actual notifying party is always external.

setup.description: Push FNOL state into orphan path so the user lands on Loss page directly

preconditions.text: Left navigation pane shows 4 steps: Loss (active), Parties, Location, Summary
Notifier section visible with exactly 2 radio options: Broker, Insured

expectedUI.description: Loss information page with Notifier radio + dynamic field — no Internal option
visualCues: Section heading 'Notifier' between Reason and Notes
Radio group: Broker / Insured only (Broker default) — no third 'Internal' option
Broker selected: 'Search broker' button opens the Name management modal (filters + table + Add Selected)
Insured selected: single labelled free-text input
Selected broker shows as a card with Legal name + IPM id + Change/Remove actions

howToTest.trigger: Scroll the Loss form, observe the Notifier section
howToTest.expectedResult: Exactly two radio options render (Broker, Insured) — no Internal

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Left navigation shows Loss / Parties / Location / Summary for orphan flow
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The FNOL **left navigation** shows four steps for the orphan path: `Loss` (/fnol/skeleton-create), `Parties` (/fnol/skeleton-parties), `Location` (/fnol/skeleton-location), and `Summary` (/fnol/skeleton-summary). Re-uses the existing FnolStepperComponent.

setup.description: Same as AC-01 — orphan path active

preconditions.text: Clicking Next advances Loss → Parties → Location → Summary, marking each prior step completed

expectedUI.description: Sidebar stepper with four visible steps
visualCues: Step 1: Loss (active dot + label)
Step 2: Parties (pending dot)
Step 3: Location (pending dot)
Step 4: Summary (pending dot)

howToTest.expectedResult: Four steps render — Loss, Parties, Location, Summary

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Loss page button reads 'Next' (was 'Create skeleton claim')
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The footer button on the Loss page is **Next** — it does *not* submit the claim, only navigates to the Parties page. Submission happens on Summary, at the end of the chain.

preconditions.text: Loss page primary button is labelled 'Next'
Clicking Next does not create the claim — it navigates to Parties

visualCues: Back button (tertiary) on the left
Next button (primary) on the right
No spinner on Next — pure navigation

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Summary page reviews Loss + Locations + Parties + Notifier and creates on Confirm
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The Summary page shows read-only review blocks — `Loss`, `Locations of loss`, `Parties`, and `Notifier` — and a **Create** button that submits the skeleton claim. Success state shows a banner with the new claim ID and a 'Go to dashboard' action.

preconditions.text: Summary page shows 'Loss' card with Client / Reason / Notes
Summary page shows 'Parties' card — empty state if none added, or a list of legal name + roles
Summary page shows 'Notifier' card with Broker or Insured (no Internal option)
Clicking Create registers the skeleton and shows success banner with claim ID

visualCues: Info banner: 'Review the details below. Click Create to register…'
Loss card with 3 fields (Client / Reason / Notes)
Locations of loss card — list or 'No locations selected.'
Parties card — list of 'Legal name · Roles' or 'No parties added.'
Notifier card with Broker or Insured (never Internal)
Footer: Back + Create

howToTest.expectedResult: Success banner shows the new skeleton claim ID; toast 'Skeleton claim created'

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Parties page starts empty, carries over the notifier broker, and supports adding another party — never mandatory
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The **Parties** page does *not* pre-populate from a policy — there is none for an orphan claim, so it starts empty except for the broker carried over from the notifier screen (if one was selected there). The user can **Add party** to cover cases like a different insurer reaching out about the claim. Parties are **not mandatory** — Next always works, same rule as the regular claim flow.

setup.description: Orphan path with a broker already selected on the notifier screen, to verify carry-over

preconditions.text: Parties page shows only the carried-over broker (or an empty state if no broker was selected)
'Add party' opens the party search modal — same modal used by the regular claim flow
Next is enabled with zero parties present

expectedUI.description: Flat party list (no claim/section tree — there is no claim hierarchy without a policy)
visualCues: Toolbar: 'Number of parties: N' + 'Add party' button
Broker from the notifier screen appears as the first row, role 'Broker'
Empty state reads 'No parties yet.' + 'Use "Add party" to get started — this step is optional.'
Row kebab: View details / Edit role / Remove
Footer Next is never disabled by party count

howToTest.trigger: Select a broker on the notifier screen, click Next, observe Parties; then click 'Add party' and search for another insurer
howToTest.expectedResult: Broker row appears automatically; added party appears and highlights; clicking Next with any number of parties (including zero) proceeds to Location

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Location step uses manual entry only — no 'select from contract location' option
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The **Location** step lets the handler enter a loss location manually (address or coordinates) — it cannot use the standard Location Manager MFE because that depends on a linked policy/contract, which does not exist for an orphan claim. There is no 'select from contract location' option anywhere on this step.

setup.description: Orphan path — Location step reached after Parties

preconditions.text: 'Add location' opens the manual-entry modal directly — no intermediate policy-location search step
Manual-entry modal has address fields plus optional latitude/longitude

expectedUI.description: Same look-and-feel as the regular claim flow's location screen, minus the contract-location path
visualCues: Section heading 'Locations of loss'
Empty state: 'Where did the loss occur?' + 'Add location' button
'Add location' → manual-entry modal (address line 1/2, postal code, city, country, province) with an 'Optional details' section for property ID + latitude/longitude
No policy-location search modal or 'select from contract' affordance anywhere on this step
Added location renders as a table row with Edit / Remove via kebab

howToTest.trigger: Click 'Add location', fill the manual-entry form (optionally expand 'Optional details' for coordinates), save
howToTest.expectedResult: Location appears as a row in the table; no contract/policy location option was ever shown
